chapter: Massey Hall, race and the record business
title: Record companies hiding that jazz sells
summary: Festival crowds versus what record companies admit; jazz sells again and again and costs less to make than rock.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: The record companies. I feel that not only my music, but Duke's music, by most -- even the big record companies, that they try and make jazz like it doesn't sell.

For instance, you go to a jazz festival in Newport, they have 15,000, 20,000 people. I mean, when it's run successfully, without the riots, which is also done by the police. And then you have one here in Long Island. They used to have a festival out on Long Island, right?
Then you have another one in California, and they all have 15,000, 20,000 people at them. They're not the same crowd going around from festival to festival.

Yet, you can't get a record company to admit they sell to the half that many fans. I think that they purposely don't push so-called American jazz, because jazz is the kind of music that sells and resells again.
Your The records are still in the catalogs.
People buy it over and over again when they wear it out.
Same as If I had Bartok's Violin Concerto, it would have wore out, I'd buy another one.
Do you feel that the record companies have been honest with you, as far as numbers are concerned?
Not just me, man. I'm talking about all the --
That's the system, where they make jazz look like it's not a powerful business.

Well, jazz records cost a great deal less to make. You can go in and make a great jazz record in three-hour sessions. Some of those rock and roll albums, the production costs before they even get the record on the street is $100,000.

And they may sell a lot of records, but they don't make as much money, probably, on some of those things, even if they are million dollar sellers. It takes them so many records to recoup their investment, that I'm sure jazz is very profitable for a company like Atlantic.
